movie.title: Across the Hall
movie.overview: A documentary amplifying the voices of women marginalized by Brazil’s penal system. It follows Érica and Núbia, who met in prison and forged a deep bond that endures beyond the bars. Now on parole, they recount stories of abuse, overcrowding, and the erasure of their identities as women. Lacking legal support, they confront these hardships with courage and humor. The film exposes the invisibility and neglect faced by incarcerated women, challenging sensationalist portrayals and urging empathy. It seeks to humanize their experiences, sparking debate about the cruelty and inefficacy of the penal system, and reclaiming the dignity of lives society too easily forgets.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: This powerful documentary follows former cellmates Érica and Núbia as they navigate life on parole while shedding light on the systemic neglect, abuse, and dehumanization faced by incarcerated women in Brazil.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Across the Hall amplifies the often-silenced voices of women navigating Brazil's harsh penal system. Focusing on Érica and Núbia—two women who forged a resilient friendship behind bars—the documentary reveals the grim reality of prison life, including overcrowding, systemic abuse, and a lack of legal representation. Now on parole, the duo confront their past and present hardships with remarkable courage and humor. Ultimately, the film challenges sensationalist media narratives and demands empathy and reform for marginalized women forgotten by society.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Across the Hall provides an intimate and urgent look into the lived experiences of women affected by Brazil's punitive criminal justice system. The narrative centers on Érica and Núbia, who initially met while serving time in prison and built an enduring bond of sisterhood to survive the harsh conditions inside. Now out on parole, they reflect on their time behind bars, painting a harrowing picture of institutional neglect, severe overcrowding, physical and psychological abuse, and the systematic erasure of their identities as women. Deprived of basic human rights and adequate legal counsel, the two women rely on their shared strength, resilience, and wit to rebuild their lives in the outside world. Through candid interviews and deeply personal storytelling, the documentary exposes the profound invisibility of incarcerated women, contrasting their true stories against sensationalized media portrayals. The film highlights how the penal system fails to rehabilitate, opting instead to punish and marginalize those who are already vulnerable. By contrasting systemic cruelty with the warmth and humor of its subjects, the film humanizes a deeply stigmatized population. In doing so, it serves as a critical call to action, demanding structural reform and asserting the dignity of lives that society frequently discards.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Across the Hall is a poignant documentary that delves into the systemic flaws of Brazil's penal system through the eyes of those who have survived it. Centering on the enduring bond between Érica and Núbia, two women who met while incarcerated and bonded over their shared struggle, the film offers a raw, spoiler-free look at the realities of female imprisonment. From facing overcrowding and institutional mistreatment to enduring the erasure of their womanhood, Érica and Núbia recount their journey with extraordinary resilience and humor. Now navigating the challenges of parole without sufficient structural support, their story exposes the broader societal neglect of marginalized women and invites viewers to reconsider the true cost and efficacy of the justice system.
